what: THE COMPLETE LIST of fields the crystal-A2 mint pipeline does not fold into the committed core module: everything the emitted artifact carries that the minted and registered `ir_<chain>_module` does not. One list, so the finite set is visible at once instead of being rediscovered one counterexample at a time. A row records what CLOSED it: `kind` is `compared` when the slot is erased from the module but pinned in the chain's tag table and checked by `ir_mint::project`, `refused` when reading it is now a hard error, `erased` when it is a justified erasure, and `unwitnessed` when one reader structurally cannot see it. As of 2026-08-20 there are SEVEN `compared`, TWO `refused` and TWO `unwitnessed`, and no row is `erased`.
why:
Each row below is a claim boundary. `read_by` names the lane that reads the row, or says NOTHING. An unwritten claim boundary is how the 2026-08-20 callee-namespace collision survived: it was an erasure nobody had written down, in a slot two writers each assumed the other owned. Writing them down is what made the closures possible at all -- a row that carries a CONSTRUCTED WITNESS (a pair of emitted bodies denoting different programs that the gate accepted as one) is a row that can be turned into a runnable acceptance test.

The second lesson of 2026-08-20 is sharper and is the reason `cc-and-linkage` reads the way it does: a row can be WRONG. That row said for months that the producer printed neither the calling convention nor the linkage, and therefore that no text reader could ever witness either. The producer prints both. Nobody had opened `trust_ir::display`. A claim boundary written from memory is a claim boundary that can rot into an excuse, so every `erased` and `unwitnessed` row now owes a citation to the producer's own source, quoted, and not a recollection of it.
how_this_file_is_kept_true: `crystal_a2_mint`'s blind-slot lane parses this file and, for every row, asserts that each `anchors` entry still occurs VERBATIM in the named source file. A change that closes an erasure therefore BREAKS the row that claims it -- which is what happened twice on 2026-08-20: the first closure broke four anchors, and the second broke `spans-and-tags`'s `strip_comment` signature the moment the clause reader started returning content as well as kinds. The file could not be quietly outlived either time. Rows carrying a `witness` name a test that CONSTRUCTS the indistinguishable pair; for a `compared` or `refused` row that test asserts the pair is REJECTED, and it is the acceptance test for the closure.
not_covered_by_this_file: Fields that are not erased but are UNWITNESSED BY ONE READER are a different thing and live in the mint record's ledger (`ir_<chain>.mint.json`) plus `mask_text_unwitnessed`. `switch.exhaustive_enum_unreachable` is the only such field today; it is listed here too, marked `kind: unwitnessed`, so one read covers both categories.

slots.why_the_old_justification_did_not_hold:
The row previously justified the erasure on three grounds. Two were true and one was the wrong theorem.
(1) STRUCTURAL -- `IRFunc` has no type field, so a signature index has no slot to occupy. TRUE, and it is a fine reason to keep it out of the MODULE. It is not a reason to accept two artifacts that differ in it.
(2) SEMANTIC -- `ir_exec_callind_sig_irrelevant` proves `ir_exec` returns the same IRConfig at any two signature indices. TRUE, and about a DIFFERENT OBJECT: that theorem is about `callindirect`'s operand, an index inside the fragment. This row is about the FUNCTION'S OWN HEADER signature, which the fragment does not contain and the theorem does not mention. The row's own text conceded the gap -- `the only place the fragment carries a signature index at all is callindirect's operand` -- and then used the theorem anyway. The theorem is kept as an anchor of the `switch`/`callindirect` inertness set; it is no longer cited as this row's justification.
(3) MEASURED -- `the index moves on every producer change with no instruction changed, which is why gating it would be a false-alarm generator.` NEARLY true and not decisive. Re-measured 2026-08-20 from the committed `generated/ir_mint.producer_ab.json`, reader A's independent record over three producer dumps: 9 of 11 chained bodies moved their `functy` index; 11 of 11 moved their `@func.N`. The drift rate is the same as the callee namespace's -- and the callee namespace IS pinned. Drift was never a reason not to pin; it is a reason to pin in the reviewed TABLE rather than in the module, which is exactly what the `enums`, `structs` and `funcs` lanes already do. Both designated chains are in the 2 that did NOT move: `has_cubical_layer` and `level_is_zero` are `artifact_functy_id: [0, 0, 0]` across all three dumps, so neither pin would have fired on any of the three producer changes that have actually happened.
slots.producer_invariance: NONE, deliberately, and this is the one lane where the M7 bargain is paid in full rather than dodged. There is no canonicalisation available: a body has exactly ONE header signature, so first-use interning would map every body to `functy#0` and pin nothing, and the emitted text carries no signature table to resolve the index through. It is therefore pinned VERBATIM -- exactly as the `funcs` lane pins a callee's `@func.N` -- and a producer re-interning is a reviewed one-line re-pin. The refusal PRINTS both the artifact's index and the pin so that re-pin is an edit and not an investigation. The cost is recorded where it is paid: `functy.N` was removed from the two `pure renumbering must not fire` negative controls (`crystal_a2_mint/mutation.rs`, `crystal_a2_mint/interface.rs`), and the second of those now ASSERTS that a moved signature index fires.

Nothing in this repo says what `functy.0` IS -- neither reader can print `(ptr) -> bool` -- so the pin establishes that two dumps name the same table entry, not that the entry means what a reader thinks. Resolving it needs reader A to record the resolved `FuncTy` from the artifact's own type table, which is a build item and is written down here rather than assumed away.

slots.consequence: The CONTENT erasure is deliberate and load-bearing, and stays: the `#loc` file index is a whole-crate table that renumbers with no instruction changed, and `Module::stable_digest` excludes it upstream for the same reason. Erasing it is what makes the core digest producer-invariant. What was WRONG before 2026-08-20 is that the erasure was unbounded -- every `  ; #...` suffix was dropped whatever it said -- so a producer that started annotating an instruction with something trust-bearing would have been erased in silence. That is the exact failure the `exhaustive_enum_unreachable` flag demonstrates one level in. The kind set is now an allowlist of five, each inert for a stated reason, and an unlisted kind is a refusal.

The reader's own `CLAUSE_KINDS` allowlist refuses an unlisted kind. `scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py` still reports `#loc` drift as the AMBER `loc-file-index` class.
slots.the_content_question_2026_08_20: ASKED: can clause CONTENT be compared modulo renumbering, the way `Tags::canon_ty` resolves `enum.13 -> enum#0`? ANSWERED, per kind, because the five kinds are not one thing. (1) `#loc` is `<file> <line> <col>` (`trust-ir/src/display.rs`: `write!(f, "  ; #loc: {} {} {}", span.file, span.line, span.col)`). Only `file` is a renumbering -- a whole-crate table index, exactly the shape `canon_ty` handles, and it COULD be first-use interned through a new `files` lane. `line` and `col` are not a renumbering at all: they are the source coordinates, they move when the SOURCE moves (any edit above the function shifts every line), and there is no table to resolve them through. The most that survives both motions is the loc PARTITION -- which instructions share a position -- and that is invariant under a file re-intern and under a uniform line shift, and measurable. (2) The decision is NO for `loc`, `scope` and `names`, and the reason is a measurement rather than a preference: two bodies differing only in `#loc` content DENOTE THE SAME PROGRAM (`the_producer_clause_content_is_compared_and_the_other_four_are_measured_inert` constructs the pair and requires it to be ACCEPTED and to project to one core module). A gate that refused that pair would be refusing something it has no business refusing, which is how a lane gets switched off. The lineage half of the fact already has a lane -- `scripts/crystal_fixture_freshness.py`'s AMBER `loc-file-index` class -- and that is the right home for it. (3) `#proof` stays erased for a different reason, stated rather than assumed: it is a claim ABOUT the body, not part of it, and `ir_exec` has no proof notion, so its content cannot change what the module computes. (4) `#producer` is the ONE kind whose content is now COMPARED. It names WHICH COMPILER emitted the function, it does not renumber, and erasing it while claiming the body is the one `trust` emitted was the one content erasure this lane could not justify. It was free until 2026-08-20: a body annotated `; #producer: llvm` projected to the same core module and the same interface as the same body annotated `; #producer: trust`, and the gate accepted both.
slots.residual: The file index inside `#loc` is a renumbering that COULD be canonicalised and is not. Nothing depends on it and nothing claims it is inert for any reason other than that debug-info coordinates cannot change what a module computes -- which is why the honest classification of the remaining erasure is LINEAGE, not semantics.

It suppresses each only when it holds its default, and `trust_ir::parser`'s `try_parse_calling_conv` and `is_func_prefix` read both back, so the encoding round-trips and ABSENCE IS A VALUE. The `rustcc` at the head of every committed fixture has been the calling convention the whole time. This is the same failure class as the `exhaustive_enum_unreachable` transcription -- a claim about the producer that nobody had checked against the producer -- and it is the reason this file exists.

The one convention the fragment DOES carry, on `callindirect`, is proved inert: `ir_exec_callind_conv_irrelevant` proves `ir_exec` returns the same IRConfig at any two conventions. slots.the_decision_2026_08_20: The three options were: PRINT it, DROP it from the model, or record it as permanently blind. The answer is NONE OF THE THREE ALONE -- it is KEPT in the model, kept unprinted, and PROVED INERT. Dropping it would lose a field the artifact carries and the model can hold, and would move every registered term. Printing it is a producer-side change in the `trust` repo that this lane cannot land safely and that would not help until every fixture is re-dumped; it remains the right long-term fix and is the only thing that would give the slot a second in-repo witness. So the slot stays single-witness -- reader A, the artifact binary -- and what was a COMMENT (`eval_ir_machine` drops the flag, so no theorem moved) is now a kernel-checked theorem: `ir_exec_switch_exh_irrelevant` proves `ir_exec m (IRInst.switch v d da cs Bool.true) rs s` and `... Bool.false ...` are the SAME IRConfig, at every module, state, selector, default, argument list and case list. The flag's value is therefore a LINEAGE fact about which module was emitted, and provably not a fact about what that module computes -- which is exactly why the hand transcription being WRONG about it moved no theorem, now stated as a proof instead of an observation.

Until then this is a single-assumption slot whose only defence is that two readers derive it differently and are compared.

slots.artifact_carries: Whatever the file holds after `}`. A real trust-ir module text carries the rest of the module there: more functions, the `global` declarations, the `file` table, the type tables.
slots.core_carries: Nothing, and until 2026-08-20 nothing SAID nothing. `Reader::run` matched the first line equal to `}` and `break`, so the remainder was neither read nor refused.
slots.erased_by: Nothing, any more. A non-blank line after the close is a hard refusal naming the line, and a body that runs out without a close is refused as truncated. Trailing BLANK lines are still accepted, so this refuses content and not whitespace.

slots.the_counterexample_2026_08_20: CONSTRUCTED, and it is the sharper of the third pass's two. Measured before the fix, ALL FOUR accepted and all four projecting to the IDENTICAL core module as the one-function body: `m::f` followed by a whole second function `m::g`; `m::f` followed by a `global` declaration; followed by a `file` table; followed by arbitrary prose. And the sharp one -- a `}` appearing MID-BODY truncated the function and dropped every instruction after it IN SILENCE, so `bb0(%0: ptr): unreachable } %9 = load i64, ptr %0  ret %9` read as a body whose only instruction is `unreachable`.
slots.why_this_one_matters_more_than_a_missing: Because it is the assumption the rest of this file rests on. `blind_slots.rs`'s own module docs say the list cannot be PROVED complete and that what holds completeness up is both readers being TOTAL-OR-REFUSING -- `an unrecognised construct is a hard error in both readers, so a field can only be erased by a line someone wrote to erase it, and those lines are what the anchors point at.` A `break` that ignores the remainder of the input is precisely a reader that is not total, and it erases things nobody enumerated, so no anchor could ever have pointed at them. The nine rows above were each a field somebody chose to drop. This one was the reader quietly ending early.
slots.consequence: CLOSED 2026-08-20 by REFUSAL, which is the right close for a reader whose contract is ONE body per text: there is nothing in a second function for a one-function projection to say, so the honest answer is to stop rather than to ignore. If a chain ever needs to project a whole module, this refusal is the thing that has to be lifted deliberately, together with projecting the function list.
slots.read_by: `crystal_a2_mint`'s blind-slot lane, which constructs all five bodies and requires each to be refused, AND requires trailing blank lines to still be accepted so the refusal is about content rather than whitespace.
slots.live_on_chains: none of the sixteen committed fixtures carries anything after its close -- which is exactly why this was latent, and exactly the position `global-index` was in before it was closed.
slots.residual: Reader A is unaffected: it projects one `trust_ir::Function` out of a decoded module and never sees text, so it could not have had this defect and gains nothing from the fix. The two readers were therefore NOT in agreement about what the fixture file means, and nothing had noticed.

justification_standard: A row that stays `erased` or `unwitnessed` must justify itself with a KERNEL-CHECKED THEOREM, a MEASURED FACT, or a QUOTED LINE of the producer's source -- never with a recollection. The standard for a theorem is `ir_ty_is_agg_enum_any` (`spec/core_spec/eval_ir_ops.rs`), which proves `ir_ty_is_agg (IRTy.enum_ n) = Bool.true` at EVERY whole-crate id and is why a type-table renumbering cannot reach the value the machine computes; `ir_exec_switch_exh_irrelevant`, `ir_exec_callind_conv_irrelevant` and `ir_exec_callind_sig_irrelevant` (`spec/core_spec/eval_ir_machine.rs`) are the same standard for three dropped operands. And a theorem must be about THE OBJECT THE ROW IS ABOUT: `functy-index` cited `ir_exec_callind_sig_irrelevant` for four months, which proves something true about `callindirect`'s operand and nothing at all about the function's own header signature. That mismatch is what let a variadic and a non-variadic function be accepted as one program.
